baseline_gamma_vs_gamma_across_studies.note: hugely dispersed -- OSD-498 and OSD-508 are two accessions of the same published experiment and correlate at 0.045, so full-profile correlation is dominated by study-level noise

interpretation: NO EVIDENCE, AND NO POWER TO EXCLUDE. The matched within-OSD-320 comparison of gamma against Fe-56 HZE gives rho 0.31, at the 20.0th percentile of the gamma-versus-gamma baseline (mean 0.42, range [0.045, 0.641]; one-sided p = 0.25) -- inside that distribution, not below it. But the baseline itself is the problem: two accessions of the SAME published experiment correlate at 0.04, so study-to-study variance is as large as any quality effect this design could detect, and response magnitude does not explain the scatter (rho 0.16, p 0.42). With 8 radiation contrasts these data neither support radiation quality as the reason spaceflight shows no signature nor rule it out. What is not in doubt is dose: the model was trained at 100 Gy and the ISS delivers at most 2.485 cGy, a factor of ~4024. All radiation qualities fire both arms of the decoder, consistent with a conserved DNA-damage core.

matched_pair_vs_baseline.criterion: quality claim requires the matched pair in the lower tail (p < 0.05), not merely below the baseline mean

matched_test.design: same study, same 8-day-old Ws/atm-1 seedlings, same facility (BNL), same 7 Gy/min dose rate and harvest times; Cs-137 gamma (100 Gy) vs 1 GeV/n Fe-56 HZE (30 Gy)

power.note: Two accessions of the same published experiment (OSD-498, OSD-508) correlate at the value above. That is the reproducibility floor of this measurement, and any quality effect would have to exceed the study-to-study variance to be visible above it. Response magnitude does not explain the scatter, so it is not a nuisance that could be regressed out.
